correctness.rationale: One-point Henson graph types are exactly triangle-free neighborhoods. For line graphs of cubic triangle-free ladders this complements to edge covers. A four-state transfer enumerates the weighted covers, and its row-swap antisymmetric line has site eigenvalue \(-u_i\); hence trace(I-J) equals exactly \(2(-1)^n\) times the product of all rail-pair weights. The proof covers all \(n\ge4\) with quantifiers and boundary seam explicit. The standalone checker independently verifies exact coefficient spectra widths 4 through 6, Henson-neighborhood enumeration widths 4 and 5, heterogeneous weight specializations widths 4 and 5, and transfer identities through width 12. These tests do not replace the all-order transfer proof.

value.rationale: The result supplies an exact complete multivariate boundary-response law for two globally nonisomorphic cubic families with arbitrarily heterogeneous rung activities, rather than an isolated table or specialization. In the logical setting it locates all loss of reconstructive information in a single extremal coefficient of the entire named-parameter type spectrum. Its exact structural mechanism is a one-dimensional antisymmetric transfer sector; this motivates further comparisons in finite-model type invariants and weighted counting.
